title: A Sober Look at LLMs for Material Discovery: Are They Actually Good for Bayesian Optimization Over Molecules?

metadata.authors: Kristiadi A, Strieth-Kalthoff F, Skreta M, Poupart P, Aspuru-Guzik A, Pleiss G

abstract:
A Sober Look at LLMs for Material Discovery:
Are They Actually Good for Bayesian Optimization Over Molecules?
Agustinus Kristiadi 1 Felix Strieth-Kalthoff 2 Marta Skreta 2 1 Pascal Poupart 3 1 Al´an Aspuru-Guzik 2 1
Geoff Pleiss 4 1
https://github.com/wiseodd/lapeft-bayesopt
Abstract
Automation is one of the cornerstones of contem-
porary material discovery. Bayesian optimization
(BO) is an essential part of such workflows, en-
abling scientists to leverage prior domain knowl-
edge into efficient exploration of a large molecu-
lar space. While such prior knowledge can take
many forms, there has been significant fanfare
around the ancillary scientific knowledge encap-
sulated in large language models (LLMs). How-
ever, existing work thus far has only explored
LLMs for heuristic materials searches. Indeed,
recent work obtains the uncertainty estimate—an
integral part of BO—from point-estimated, non-
Bayesian LLMs. In this work, we study the ques-
tion of whether LLMs are actually useful to ac-
celerate principled Bayesian optimization in the
molecular space. We take a sober, dispassionate
stance in answering this question. This is done
by carefully (i) viewing LLMs as fixed feature ex-
tractors for standard but principled BO surrogate
models and by (ii) leveraging parameter-efficient
finetuning methods and Bayesian neural networks
to obtain the posterior of the LLM surrogate. Our
extensive experiments with real-world chemistry
problems show that LLMs can be useful for BO
over molecules, but only if they have been pre-
trained or finetuned with domain-specific data.

methods.value: Compare BO performance using LLMs as fixed feature extractors versus finetuned LLMs, with domain-specific and general-purpose LLMs.

problems.value: Determine whether large language models (LLMs) are effective for accelerating Bayesian optimization (BO) in molecular space.

hypotheses.value: LLMs can provide useful features for BO over molecules when pretrained or finetuned with domain-specific data.

evidence.value: Experiments with 8 real-world chemistry problems using various LLMs show that domain-specific LLMs and finetuned LLMs improve BO performance.

conclusions.value: LLMs can be useful for BO over molecules if they are pretrained or finetuned with domain-specific data.

materials.value: A Sober Look at LLMs for Material Discovery: Are They Actually Good for Bayesian Optimization Over Molecules?

mechanisms.value: Feature extraction from LLMs for BO
Incorporation of domain-specific data in LLM training

outcomes.value: Improved BO performance with domain-specific LLMs
Better generalization of LLMs to chemistry problems with domain-specific training

failure_paths.value: failure: Using general-purpose LLMs as feature extractors for BO. Evidence: General-purpose LLMs tend to underperform compared to domain-specific LLMs.
failure: Employing in-context learning with non-Bayesian LLMs for BO. Evidence: Non-Bayesian uncertainties from in-context learning may not be optimal for the exploration-exploitation tradeoff in BO.

provenance.cross_sdl_notes: The paper provides a structured exploration of LLMs in the context of BO for molecular discovery, allowing for a clear extraction of the scientific reasoning. However, some details on the specific experimental setups and data preprocessing steps were not fully detailed, requiring some assumptions during extraction.
